title: Brown 2011: pcsa of transversus abdominis at whole (mixed, cadaver)

imaging.level_definition: whole muscle and regions (1 = most superior/anterior)

quantity.name: pcsa
quantity.definition: physiological CSA = muscle volume (mass/density) / fibre length (x cos pennation if stated)

source.authors: Brown SHM, Ward SR, Cook MS, Lieber RL
source.sample: 11 formaldehyde-fixed cadavers (5 M, 6 F); elderly donors: M 71.8 (17.9) y, 174.8 cm, 67.8 kg; F 82.7 (14.5) y, 165.6 cm, 63.1 kg

how_to_simulate: Sum the PCSA (or F_max / specific tension) of all model elements of transversus abdominis, one side (or the named fascicle).
Compare with the cadaveric mean +/- SD; note specific tension and fibre-length normalisation used by the source.
protocol.notes: Table 1 reports mean ± SEM (n=11): SEM stored in "se", sd empty. Regional PCSAs do not sum to whole-muscle PCSA in all cases (whole RA PCSA = largest region?). Model-predicted sarcomere operating ranges (Figs 4-5) not stored.

extraction.check_notes: Table 1 rows re-read from text (single-line rows).
